function: C-DRCNN denoises the received pilot tensor before PARAFAC/TALS decomposition, improving UE-RIS channel parameter and channel estimation, which also feeds multiuser positioning and environment mapping; pp. 4-8.
system: RIS-assisted uplink multiuser mmWave MIMO-OFDM: BS 4x4 UPA, two users with 4x4 UPAs, passive reflecting RIS 6x6 with low-resolution phases, 28 GHz, no UE-BS LoS; pp. 3, 5, 9.
method: Complex-valued deep residual CNN (7 layers, 64 filters, BN, cReLU) trained offline in a supervised way to estimate noise, followed by non-learned PARAFAC/TALS; Adam, 120 epochs; pp. 6-7, 10.
data_channel: Simulated Saleh-Valenzuela UE-RIS channel (two NLoS paths per user), datasets generated from Eqs. 23-25: 2000 samples per SNR level, 90% training and 10% test; pp. 3, 9-10.
test_conditions: Held-out 10% of generated data per SNR level; SNR swept and time blocks B (16, 24, 32) varied, datasets built 'under specific simulation parameters'; pp. 10-12.
baselines: Non-learned ALS (alternating least squares) tensor algorithm without DL; noise-free reference line; no learned baseline; pp. 10-11.
metrics: RMSE of channel parameters (angles, delay, gain), RMSE of user and scattering-point positions, NMSE of UE-RIS channel, loss curves; versus SNR; Figs. 3-9, pp. 9-13.
q1_support: p. 3: "the classical Saleh–Valenzuela channel model [33]". Custom simulator following a textbook model (two NLoS paths per user, p. 9); no 3GPP TR 38.901, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "The data set contains 2000 samples for each SNR level under specific simulation parameters"; "90% is used for training and 10% is used for testing". Tests sweep SNR and the number of time blocks B (p. 12), but no test of the trained network on unseen conditions or after adaptation is reported.
q3_support: p. 10: "we compare the proposed algorithm with the existing ALS algorithm". ALS is the conventional iteration without DL (p. 11); no earlier learned method is simulated (the DL works [25]-[27] appear only in the introduction, p. 2).
q4_support: p. 3: "the complexity and hardware consumption of the proposed algorithm can be accordingly adjusted" is qualitative; p. 11: "it takes less time and computational resources to train the C-DRCNN". No order of complexity, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 10: "The data set required by the C-DRCNN is generated by the formulas (23)–(25)". Synthetic self-generated data; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 2: the learned C-DRCNN denoises the received pilot tensor inside a PARAFAC/TALS pipeline, and the paper reports the NMSE of the UE-RIS channel (Fig. 5, p. 11) next to positioning RMSE; channel estimation in an ISAC system is area 2. Positioning and mapping are computed geometrically from the estimated parameters (p. 8), outside the learned part, so the reviewer should confirm that the denoiser counts as the learned component and that the function is not positioning alone. p. 11 states that "When the environment is extended to more users and more complex environments, the proposed algorithm still works" without any result, so q2 stays 0. ALS is the only baseline and it is non-learned.
